feed.title: Omacus updates
feed.subtitle: Every release of Omacus, in plain words.

entry.title: v0.2.15 — Keep a copy of everything
entry.content:
Export everything in Settings saves your pages, folders, settings, and Recently deleted in one file. Locked pages are included, and they stay locked.

Exported pages have slimmer margins, so more of the sheet is the note itself. A code block sits with the text, in a monospace face, and a long line wraps instead of running off the page.

On a phone, the top bar matches the page, with no tint in the Home Screen app. Settings opens below the top bar, and the sidebar lists your pages cleanly. The privacy note is in About.

  • Settings shows the hash of this web app. The same hash is on the release page, so you can confirm this copy matches the one that was published.
  • A locked page is named Locked page in the list, and a reference to it stays locked until you open it.
  • On iPhone, Add to Home Screen is offered as soon as the app opens.

Build hash: 044a18c0edaae169ad716fc600fa0eec78ea5861ebca893bceddac6941d7c761

Settings shows this hash. This copy matches the release when the two hashes are the same.

entry.title: v0.2.13 — A clearer app on your phone
entry.content:
The top bar is a solid strip, the sidebar shows the version and Settings, and the page menu only lists what you can do with that page.

  • Locking a page asks you to choose a password, then locks it. Save that password in a password manager.
  • Removing a lock asks for the password and keeps the page.

entry.title: v0.2.12 — The web app works offline
entry.content:
The web app at app.omacus.com keeps working with no connection after the first visit, and a new version asks before it reloads so an unsaved edit is not lost. What's new is a short title and a sentence or two, on the updates page and in the app.

  • Opening omacus.com/app brings your saved pages along, then opens the app.
  • Opening or switching a page no longer draws a frame around it.

entry.title: v0.2.11 — See every update in one place
entry.content: The updates page lists each version in plain words, newest first. What's new in the app opens the same page.

entry.title: v0.2.10 — A cleaner, calmer look
entry.content:
The app and the website share one quiet look, in light and dark. Type, spacing, and colour come from the same choices, so a screen matches the site.

  • Settings, About, and dialogs use the same frames and buttons

entry.title: v0.2.9 — Edit names like any other text
entry.content:
Renaming a value, a folder, or a handle is a normal text field: you can select, paste, and use the arrow keys. Hovering a value such as @trip.total shows one card, with the amount and the page it comes from.

  • Press F2, or choose Rename. Enter keeps the name, and Esc puts it back

entry.title: v0.2.8 — Lock pages and folders with a password
entry.content:
A page or a folder stays locked until you type the password. Without it, the notes and the numbers cannot be read.

  • Lock one page, or a whole folder, from its menu

entry.title: v0.2.7 — Use a number from another page
entry.content:
Type @trip.total to use a value from Trip Budget on the page you are writing. Change the number there, and every page that uses it follows.

  • Typing @ lists your pages, then the names on the one you pick
  • Renaming a name, or the page's handle, updates every use
  • A missing page stays a quiet hint

entry.title: v0.2.6 — Use your pages from the terminal
entry.content:
Calculate a line, or a whole page, from the command line. You can list, create, and export pages, and tools such as Cursor and Claude can do the same.

  • Export a page as notes, or as a PDF

entry.title: v0.2.5 — Organize pages into folders
entry.content: Drag a page into a folder in the sidebar, and keep a long list in order. Folders open and close, and a new folder starts from the sidebar.

entry.title: v0.2.4 — Rename a name everywhere it appears
entry.content:
Rename a value and every line that uses it updates, in one undo. Enter keeps the name, and Esc cancels.

  • Press F2, use the right-click menu, or choose Rename when you hover
  • On a phone, long-press the name
  • A name that is already used on the page is refused

entry.title: v0.2.3 — Answers update as you type on a phone
entry.content:
A line such as groceries = 100 shows 100 right away, and groceries * 2 shows 200. Lines below the one you edit stay current.

  • A dash or a curly quote still calculates, so 100 – 20 is 80

entry.title: v0.2.2 — Preview and PDF stay in step with the page
entry.content:
Scrolling a long page scrolls the preview too. The PDF keeps your lines, blank lines, and comments, and uses the page title as its file name.

  • Settings opens as a tab beside About
  • Check for updates can run again after it finishes

entry.title: v0.2.1 — Clearer printing, and Settings from the sidebar
entry.content:
Print and Export PDF set the page like a short document, with margins and headings, and a line is not split across a page. The gear at the bottom of the sidebar opens Settings.

  • A value you hover stays on one line, inside the window
  • An answer on the line keeps its brackets, for example [ $48 ]

entry.title: v0.2.0 — Preview a page, and see a value when you hover
entry.content:
Ctrl+P shows the page as notes, with each answer beside its line. Hover a name, or a number such as 1.5k, to see its value, and click an answer to copy it.

  • The web app opens when you are offline, and says so if exchange rates may be old
  • Settings chooses the theme, where answers sit, and whether to check for updates
  • A list or a heading can hold a calculation, so - hotel = 3 nights * $180 names hotel
  • The sidebar, the docs, and the app say page

entry.title: v0.1.29 — Sidebar icons line up
entry.content: The new-page button, the sidebar button, and help sit on one line with the rows beside them.

entry.title: v0.1.28 — Open a deleted page before restoring it
entry.content: A page in Recently deleted can be opened so you can read it, then restored. A long name stays on one row.

entry.title: v0.1.27 — The page list keeps your place
entry.content: Moving through the page list with the keyboard no longer sends focus somewhere else.

entry.title: v0.1.26 — Sum a few amounts, and bring a page back
entry.content:
sum(), avg(), min(), and max() take a list of amounts, including units and currencies. Deleting a page asks first, and Recently deleted can bring it back.

  • The page list is Ctrl+J (Cmd+J on a Mac)
  • An unknown name stays a quiet hint, once you pause
  • A long page opens reliably on a Mac

entry.title: v0.1.25 — Millions and billions on an amount
entry.content: After a currency symbol, m and mm mean million, and b means billion. $2m is two million dollars, not a length.

entry.title: v0.1.24 — Plan runway and a round
entry.content: Divide the cash you have by monthly spend to see how many months you can keep going. Write a round as an amount at a valuation to see the stake you give up.

entry.title: v0.1.23 — Labels stay words
entry.content:
A label in front of an amount, such as Groceries $80, stays a label. On a phone, the page stays still while you type, and the page list does not jump.

  • Omacus can be installed on a Mac with Homebrew
  • A rate such as $85/hour, or a percentage, no longer breaks the total beside it
  • After a currency symbol, b means billions

entry.title: v0.1.22 — Percentages follow the order you wrote
entry.content: 100 + 10% * 2 is 120. The percentage is applied in the same order as the rest of the line.

entry.title: v0.1.21 — Totals that work inside a line
entry.content:
total * 1.08 and total in EUR use the total of the block above, not only a line that says total by itself. Dollars and plain numbers in that total add together.

  • A line that is only a unit name, such as kg, shows nothing
  • A name you defined as total still wins over the block total

entry.title: v0.1.20 — Behind-the-scenes improvements
entry.content: Nothing you see in the app changed.

entry.title: v0.1.19 — Windows opens on more computers
entry.content: Omacus starts on a Windows PC that does not have a newer graphics driver. The first line gets the same time to finish as any other line.

entry.title: v0.1.18 — Install on Windows in one click
entry.content:
The Windows setup installs Omacus for you, with no admin prompt, and adds it to Start. On a Mac, the download opens to a window with the app and an Applications folder.

  • Or install from a terminal with one line, on Windows or anywhere else

entry.title: v0.1.17 — Answers appear as they're worked out
entry.content: You see each line's answer as it finishes, instead of waiting for the whole page. Copying an answer no longer freezes or lands late, and an impossible date says so.

entry.title: v0.1.16 — Clearer rounding, dates, and large numbers
entry.content:
$1.005 rounds to $1.01. 1.000,50 reads as one thousand and a half, 1 lakh is 100,000, and a date on its own is that date.

  • today + 3 weeks stays on the right day when the clocks change
  • I spent $40 stays $40 even when I is also a name on the page
  • $-5 is minus five dollars

entry.title: v0.1.15 — A long page stays quick
entry.content:
Editing the end of a long page recalculates that line, not every line above it. The window does not wait on the math.

  • Each line gets the same time to finish, wherever it sits on the page

entry.title: v0.1.14 — Percentages, money, and dates, more carefully
entry.content:
10% off 20% off $100 is $72. C$ and A$ read as their own currencies, and Jan 31 + 1 month stays on the calendar.

  • Halves round on the exact digits: $1.005 is $1.01
  • 10% * 200 is 20, not 2,000%

entry.title: v0.1.13 — The window stays responsive
entry.content:
A line that would take too long stops, instead of freezing the window. When a line has no answer, it can say why, quietly, in the answer's place.

  • $100 - 10% - 10% is $81
  • Tickets 2 x $14 is $28
  • A plain number added to an amount keeps the currency, so rent + 5 stays in dollars

entry.title: v0.1.12 — Answers sit on the line, including on a phone
entry.content:
Each answer sits at the end of its line, and moves below the line when there is no room. A phone no longer squeezes every line into half the screen.

  • On a phone, Share and Private live in the page menu

entry.title: v0.1.11 — Try a page on the homepage
entry.content:
The homepage can swap the demo for the real editor, on the page that was playing, without saving anything. A privacy page says what stays on your computer.

  • Share, and the page menu, sit above the page

entry.title: v0.1.10 — Share a page with a link
entry.content:
Share link copies a link that opens the page in the browser, or back in the app. The page is inside the link, so it is not sent to a server.

  • The web app keeps pages in this browser, and can open when you are offline
  • You can install it on your home screen

entry.title: v0.1.9 — Tips, splits, and how long a download takes
entry.content:
18% tip on $62, $84 split 3 ways, and 4 GB at 100 Mbps each get an answer. You can count days until a date, convert 16px in rem, and turn a colour such as #ff8800 into RGB, with a swatch.

  • Copy a page as a Markdown table
  • One download page covers every platform

entry.title: v0.1.8 — A smaller download on a Mac
entry.content: There is a download for Apple silicon and one for Intel, so each file is about half the size. Two windows stay in step, and one does not overwrite the other.

entry.title: v0.1.7 — Update checks through the day
entry.content: Omacus looks for a new version when it starts, and again every few hours while it stays open, instead of only once a day.

entry.title: v0.1.6 — Undo a deleted page, and fewer wrong answers
entry.content:
Deleting a page can be undone, and a failed save tells you instead of failing quietly. An amount in a label, such as Groceries $40, stays the amount you wrote.

  • half of 50 is 25, and 50 percent off 80 is 40
  • I spent $40 is $40, and $4 a day is four dollars a day
  • An update checks the download before it installs

entry.title: v0.1.5 — Copy a page with its answers
entry.content:
Copy with answers places each result after its line, ready to paste. You can jump to a page by its name, or by something written on it.

  • in 90 minutes, 3 hours from now in Tokyo, and 3pm + 45 min count from now
  • Exchange rates and the update check refresh while Omacus stays open

entry.title: v0.1.4 — Update in one click
entry.content:
On Windows, Update now replaces the app where it is and restarts. On a Mac, the update replaces Omacus where it already lives, instead of adding a second copy. Links in About open in the browser.

  • Help has its own window, and the version sits at the bottom of the sidebar

entry.title: v0.1.3 — Omacus tells you when a new version is out
entry.content:
A note at the bottom of the sidebar appears when a newer version is published. Update now installs it and offers to restart. Your pages and settings stay.

  • Turn the check off in settings
  • omacus --version prints the app's version

entry.title: v0.1.2 — Imperial measures, and a time on a date
entry.content:
2 imperial pints in ml converts UK pints, and CHF 300 works the same as 300 CHF. 3pm PST on Dec 1 in London uses the right offset for that date.

  • A date can be Dec 1, 1 December 2026, tomorrow, or next Monday
  • Words that only start like a day, such as Sunset, stay labels

entry.title: v0.1.1 — Percentages and units that come out right
entry.content:
6 is what % of 120 is 5%, and $100 - 20% takes the percentage off the amount. 60 km / 2 hours is a speed, and the units stay on the answer.

  • Two-word units such as nautical mile, fl oz, and sq ft
  • A block total can be saved with subtotal = total
  • The website, with docs and a download for each platform
  • The Mac installer puts Omacus in Applications

entry.title: v0.1.0 — A notepad for math
entry.content:
Omacus keeps a whole page. Every line keeps its answer, you can name a value and reuse it, and changing a line updates what follows. Pages are saved as you type, on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

  • Units, percentages, currencies, and time zones, written the way you would say them
  • The Omarchy installer asks before it adds a shortcut, and suggests Super+Ctrl+Alt+=
  • Two pages created a moment apart no longer overwrite each other
